records.source: הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־בָּבֶ֖ל אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים בְּיַ֖ד יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא׃
records.gloss: The word which spoke Yahweh concerning Babylon, concerning [the] land of [the] Chaldeans, by [the] hand of Jeremiah the prophet:
pieces: This is the word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke about Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, through Jeremiah the prophet:

L.1: The word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet:

R.1: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave through the prophet Jeremiah about Babylon and the land of the Babylonians:

decisions.choice: Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans: the great city and the country it ruled
decisions.reason: Babylon was the capital of the empire that destroyed Jerusalem in 587 BC. The Chaldeans were the people of southern Mesopotamia whose kings ruled from Babylon in Jeremiah's time, so "the land of the Chaldeans" is Babylonia as a whole (25:12). Chapters 50-51 are the last and longest of the oracles against the nations (46-51), and they end with the scroll that Seraiah read in Babylon and sank in the Euphrates (51:59-64).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Jeremiah: through Jeremiah as the messenger
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" names the one through whom a message is sent (37:2; Haggai 1:1). The heading names Jeremiah as the prophet who carried this word, in the third person, as other headings in the book do (46:1; 47:1).

decisions.choice: the heading as the Hebrew has it
alternatives: The word of the LORD which he spoke against Babylon (Greek, shorter)
decisions.reason: In the Greek translation these chapters stand earlier in the book, after 25:13, as the decision at 1:1 explains, and the heading is shorter: as far as is known from general knowledge of the Greek text, it does not have "the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet". The Hebrew text is followed. This claim about the Greek is given from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: through (B, R); Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" becomes "through". Readable says "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans, as the book does elsewhere, and puts the prophet's name first.

records.heading: Babylon's fall

records.source: הַגִּ֨ידוּ בַגּוֹיִ֤ם וְהַשְׁמִ֨יעוּ֙ וּֽשְׂאוּ־נֵ֔ס הַשְׁמִ֖יעוּ אַל־תְּכַחֵ֑דוּ אִמְרוּ֩ נִלְכְּדָ֨ה בָבֶ֜ל הֹבִ֥ישׁ בֵּל֙ חַ֣ת מְרֹדָ֔ךְ הֹבִ֣ישׁוּ עֲצַבֶּ֔יהָ חַ֖תּוּ גִּלּוּלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Declare among the nations and proclaim, and lift up [a] signal flag; proclaim, not hide [it]; say: captured [is] Babylon; put to shame [is] Bel; shattered [is] Merodach; put to shame [are] her images; shattered [are] her idols.
pieces: Announce it among the nations and proclaim it; raise a signal flag. \q Proclaim it and hide nothing. \q Say, "Babylon is taken; Bel is disgraced, Marduk is shattered. \q Her images are disgraced, her idols are shattered."

L.2: Declare among the nations and proclaim, and lift up a signal flag; \q proclaim, do not hide it; \q say, "Babylon is captured, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is shattered; \q her images are put to shame, her idols are shattered."

R.2: Tell the nations! Announce it! Raise a signal flag! \q Make it known and do not hide it. \q Say, "Babylon has been captured! Its god Bel is put to shame, and its god Marduk is broken. \q All its idols are put to shame and broken to pieces."

decisions.choice: Bel and Merodach: the chief god of Babylon, by his title and by his name
decisions.reason: Bel means "lord" and was the title of Marduk, the god of the city of Babylon (Isaiah 46:1). Merodach is the Hebrew form of the name Marduk, also found in the names Merodach-baladan (Isaiah 39:1) and Evil-merodach (2 Kings 25:27). The two lines name the same god twice, by title and by name, as poetry pairs words. When the city falls, its god is shown to be powerless.

decisions.choice: images ... idols: two words of contempt for the city's gods
decisions.reason: The first word means shaped images, things made by hand (Hosea 4:17; Isaiah 46:1). The second is a scornful word for idols, used often by Ezekiel and in Kings (1 Kings 15:12; 2 Kings 21:11); it may be linked with a word for dung, though its origin is not certain.

decisions.choice: put to shame ... shattered: disgraced and broken in terror
decisions.reason: The first verb means to be shamed, let down by what one trusted (2:36; 48:1). The second means to be shattered, and also to be broken by fear, dismayed (1:17; 48:1). Said of gods and their images, it means both: they are smashed, and their power is broken.

decisions.choice: Babylon is captured: the fall announced as already done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for a finished act. The heralds are to proclaim Babylon's fall as a fact while it is still to come, because God has decided it. The same message is to be told openly to every nation, with a flag raised as a rallying sign (4:6; 51:12, 27).

decisions.choice: Merodach (L); Marduk (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew form of the name, as Isaiah 39:1 keeps Merodach-baladan. Balanced and Readable use the god's own name, Marduk, by which he is known today. Both name the same god.

decisions.choice: Its god Bel ... its god Marduk ... All its idols
decisions.reason: Readable says that Bel and Marduk are gods, and joins the two words for idols into one line.

records.source: כִּ֣י עָלָה֩ עָלֶ֨יהָ גּ֜וֹי מִצָּפ֗וֹן הֽוּא־יָשִׁ֤ית אֶת־אַרְצָהּ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בָּ֑הּ מֵאָדָ֥ם וְעַד־בְּהֵמָ֖ה נָ֥דוּ הָלָֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: For has come up against her [a] nation from [the] north; it will make her land into [a] desolation, and not will be [an] inhabitant in it; from man and to beast they have fled, they have gone.
pieces: For a nation from the north has come up against her. \q It will turn her land into a waste, and no one will live in it. \q People and animals alike have fled and are gone.

L.3: For a nation has come up against her from the north; \q it will make her land a desolation, and no one will live in it; \q from {{gender:human|man}} to beast they have fled, they are gone.

R.3: An army from a nation in the north is attacking Babylon. \q It will turn the land into an empty waste, and no one will live there. \q People and animals will all run away.

decisions.choice: a nation from the north: the Medes and the peoples with them
decisions.reason: The attacker is named later as the kings of the Medes, with Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz (51:11, 27-28). In earlier chapters Babylon itself was the enemy from the north (1:14; 6:22). Now the nation that came from the north against Judah faces an enemy from the north in its turn.

decisions.choice: has come up ... they have fled: the future seen as already done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for a finished act, though the attack is still to come. The prophet speaks of it as certain. The "it will make" in the middle shows that it is still ahead.

decisions.choice: from human to beast: every living thing
decisions.reason: "From human to beast" covers all life in the land, people and animals together (9:9; 33:10; 51:62).

decisions.choice: is attacking ... will run away
decisions.reason: Readable puts the certain future in the present and future tense, which English uses for coming events, and says "army" for the nation on the march.

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֨ים הָהֵ֜מָּה וּבָעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה יָבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הֵ֥מָּה וּבְנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֖ה יַחְדָּ֑ו הָל֤וֹךְ וּבָכוֹ֙ יֵלֵ֔כוּ וְאֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם יְבַקֵּֽשׁוּ׃
records.gloss: In the days those and in the time that, declares Yahweh, will come [the] sons of Israel, they and [the] sons of Judah together; going and weeping they will go, and Yahweh their God they will seek.
pieces: In those days, at that time, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the {{gender:people of Judah|sons of Judah}} will come together. \q They will walk on, weeping as they go, \q and they will seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

L.4: In those days and at that time, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel will come, they and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah together; \q they will go on, going and weeping, \q and they will seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

R.4: When that time comes, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the {{gender:people of Judah|sons of Judah}} will come back together. \q They will cry as they walk along, \q and they will look for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

decisions.choice: Israel and Judah together: the two kingdoms united again
decisions.reason: Israel, the northern kingdom, was taken into exile by Assyria in 722 BC, and Judah by Babylon. Jeremiah promises that both will return as one people (3:18; 31:1, 31; Ezekiel 37:15-22). Babylon's fall opens the way home.

decisions.choice: going and weeping they will go: weeping all along the way
decisions.reason: The doubled verb shows an action that goes on. The tears are tears of sorrow for sin and of longing, as the people turn back to God (3:21; 31:9).

decisions.choice: seek the LORD: turn to him to worship and obey
decisions.reason: To seek God is to come back to him with the whole heart, not merely to look for him (29:13; Hosea 3:5).

decisions.choice: Israelites ... people of Judah
decisions.reason: The settled wording for "sons of Israel", with the traditional form as the setting's alternative; "sons of Judah" follows it.

decisions.choice: When that time comes
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two phrases for the time, which mean the same, and says "come back" because they are returning.

records.source: צִיּ֣וֹן יִשְׁאָ֔לוּ דֶּ֖רֶךְ הֵ֣נָּה פְנֵיהֶ֑ם בֹּ֚אוּ וְנִלְו֣וּ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א תִשָּׁכֵֽחַ׃ס
records.gloss: Zion they will ask, [the] way hither their faces: come, and they will join themselves to Yahweh [in a] covenant everlasting [that] not will be forgotten.
pieces: They will ask the way to Zion and set their faces toward it. \q "Come!" they will say, and they will bind themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q in a covenant that lasts forever and will never be forgotten.

L.5: They will ask for Zion, the way, with their faces [turned] toward it: \q "Come!" And they will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.

R.5: They will ask how to get to Zion and turn toward it. \q They will call to one another, "Come!" Then they will join themselves to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q by a covenant that will last forever. It will never be forgotten.

decisions.choice: "Come!" and they will join themselves: a call to one another, then what they do
alternatives: Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD (with a small change to the verb)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has a command, "Come!", followed by "and they will join themselves", not "let us join". The call is the returning people urging one another on (31:6), and the next words say what they then do. Another reading changes the second verb slightly to "let us join ourselves" and makes it all their words; the sense is close, but the Hebrew as it stands is followed.

decisions.choice: the way, their faces this way: they set out for Zion with their faces toward it
decisions.reason: To set one's face toward a place is to be determined to go there (42:15; 2 Kings 12:18). The people who once wandered (verse 6) now ask the road home and keep to it.

decisions.choice: an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten: a lasting bond with God
decisions.reason: The people broke the covenant made at Sinai and forgot God (11:10; 2:32). The new covenant God promises will last forever and will never be forgotten (31:31-34; 32:40). To join oneself to the LORD is to bind oneself to him in loyalty (Isaiah 56:3, 6).

decisions.choice: they will say (B); They will call to one another (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who calls out "Come!" (meaning decision m1). Readable makes the covenant line two short sentences.

records.source: צֹ֤אן אֹֽבְדוֹת֙ הָי֣וּ עַמִּ֔י רֹעֵיהֶ֣ם הִתְע֔וּם הָרִ֖ים שֽׁוֹבְב֑וּם מֵהַ֤ר אֶל־גִּבְעָה֙ הָלָ֔כוּ שָׁכְח֖וּ רִבְצָֽם׃
records.gloss: Sheep lost have been my people; their shepherds have caused them to wander; [on the] mountains they have turned them aside; from mountain to hill they have gone; they have forgotten their resting place.
pieces: My people have been lost sheep. \q Their shepherds have led them astray \q and let them roam on the mountains. \q They have wandered from mountain to hill \q and forgotten their resting place.

L.6: My people have been lost sheep; \q their shepherds have led them astray; \q on the mountains they have turned them aside. \q From mountain to hill they have gone; \q they have forgotten their resting place.

R.6: My people have been like lost sheep. \q Their shepherds led them the wrong way \q and made them wander on the mountains. \q They went from one mountain to another hill, \q and they forgot their home where they could rest.

decisions.choice: shepherds: the rulers of the people
decisions.reason: Kings and leaders were called the shepherds of their people, and Jeremiah blames Judah's rulers for leading the people astray (10:21; 23:1-2). The lost sheep return in verses 17 and 19.

decisions.choice: on the mountains they turned them aside: the reading marked for reading aloud
alternatives: on mountains that lead astray (written text)
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "have been" in the singular and "turning-away mountains", that is, mountains that lead astray. The reading the scribes marked for reading aloud has "have been" in the plural and "they turned them aside" (the shepherds did). The reading aloud is followed; both readings blame the people's guides and the places they went.

decisions.choice: from mountain to hill: perhaps the hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: Wandering sheep go from hill to hill looking for pasture. In Jeremiah the hills are also where the people worshiped other gods (2:20; 3:6, 23), so the picture may also point to that.

decisions.choice: their resting place: the fold where the flock lies down
decisions.reason: The word names the place where sheep lie down safely (Isaiah 65:10). In verse 7 the LORD himself is called their pasture, so the place they forgot is their life with him.

decisions.choice: like lost sheep ... their home where they could rest
decisions.reason: Readable says "like" to show the picture, and explains the resting place.

records.source: כָּל־מוֹצְאֵיהֶ֣ם אֲכָל֔וּם וְצָרֵיהֶ֥ם אָמְר֖וּ לֹ֣א נֶאְשָׁ֑ם תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֨ר חָטְא֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ נְוֵה־צֶ֔דֶק וּמִקְוֵ֥ה אֲבֽוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: All finding them have devoured them, and their enemies said: not we are guilty, because that they have sinned against Yahweh, [the] pasture of righteousness, and [the] hope of their fathers, Yahweh.
pieces: All who came upon them devoured them, \q and their enemies said, "We are not to blame, \q for they sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the pasture where they rightly belonged, \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in whom their ancestors hoped."

L.7: All who found them have devoured them, \q and their enemies have said, "We are not guilty, \q because they have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the pasture of righteousness, \q and the hope of their fathers, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.7: Everyone who found them ate them up. \q Their enemies said, "We have done nothing wrong. \q They sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who was their true pasture. \q Their ancestors put their hope in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: devoured ... not guilty: turning 2:3 around
decisions.reason: In 2:3 Israel was holy to the LORD, and all who devoured it were held guilty. Now the enemies devour Israel and say they are not guilty, because Israel has sinned. They are right about Israel's sin, but verse 18 shows that God still holds them to account.

decisions.choice: the pasture of righteousness: the LORD as the true and right home of his flock
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Jerusalem in 31:23. Here it names the LORD himself: he is the pasture where his sheep belong and are kept as they should be. The word can mean righteousness, rightness or what is true and proper.

decisions.choice: the hope of their fathers: the one their ancestors trusted
decisions.reason: The LORD is called "the hope of Israel" in 14:8 and 17:13. The enemies themselves speak as though they know whom Israel has left.

decisions.choice: the enemies' words run to the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The quotation is taken to include the reason they give. The titles of the LORD at the end may also be the prophet's own words added to theirs; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the pasture where they rightly belonged (B), their true pasture (R); not to blame (B); done nothing wrong (R)
decisions.reason: "Pasture of righteousness" means the pasture that is right and true for them (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say so in plain words. "Not guilty" is put in everyday words.

records.source: נֻ֚דוּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וּמֵאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים צֵ֑אוּ וִהְי֕וּ כְּעַתּוּדִ֖ים לִפְנֵי־צֹֽאן׃
records.gloss: Flee from [the] midst of Babylon, and from [the] land of [the] Chaldeans go out, and be like male goats before [the] flock.
pieces: Flee from Babylon! \q Get out of the land of the Chaldeans! \q Be like the male goats that lead the flock.

L.8: Flee from the midst of Babylon, \q and go out from the land of the Chaldeans, \q and be like male goats in front of the flock.

R.8: Run away from Babylon! \q Leave the land of the Babylonians! \q Be like the goats that walk in front of the flock.

decisions.choice: Flee ... go out: a call to the exiles of Israel and Judah
decisions.reason: The commands are plural, spoken to God's people living in Babylon (51:6, 45; Isaiah 48:20). They are to leave before the city falls.

decisions.choice: go out: the reading marked for reading aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "they go out"; the reading the scribes marked for reading aloud has the command "go out!", which fits the commands around it. The reading aloud is followed.

decisions.choice: male goats in front of the flock: be the first to leave
decisions.reason: When a flock is let out of the fold, the male goats push out first and lead the way. The exiles are to be first out of Babylon, not hanging back.

decisions.choice: Flee from Babylon (B); goats that walk in front (R)
decisions.reason: "The midst of" is left implied. Readable says "goats" and explains where they walk.

records.source: כִּ֣י הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֡י מֵעִיר֩ וּמַעֲלֶ֨ה עַל־בָּבֶ֜ל קְהַל־גּוֹיִ֤ם גְּדֹלִים֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן וְעָ֣רְכוּ לָ֔הּ מִשָּׁ֖ם תִּלָּכֵ֑ד חִצָּיו֙ כְּגִבּ֣וֹר מַשְׁכִּ֔יל לֹ֥א יָשׁ֖וּב רֵיקָֽם׃
records.gloss: For look, I am stirring up and bringing up against Babylon [an] assembly of nations great from [the] land of [the] north, and they will array [themselves] against her; from there she will be captured; his arrows [are] like [a] warrior bereaving; not he returns empty.
pieces: For I am about to stir up and bring against Babylon \q a horde of great nations from the north country. \q They will take up positions against her, and from there she will be taken. \q Their arrows are like a warrior who leaves families childless; \q they never come back empty.

L.9: For look, I am stirring up and bringing up against Babylon \q a company of great nations from the land of the north, \q and they will line up against her; from there she will be captured. \q Its arrows are like a warrior who bereaves; \q he does not return empty-handed.

R.9: I am going to stir up a group of great nations from the north. \q I will bring them to attack Babylon. \q They will get ready for battle, and they will capture the city. \q Their arrows will be like a soldier who leaves families without children. \q Every arrow will find its mark.

decisions.choice: a company of great nations: the Medes and their allies
decisions.reason: Babylon fell in 539 BC to the Persian king Cyrus, whose empire joined the Persians and the Medes and drew troops from many peoples. Chapter 51 names the Medes, with Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz, peoples of the mountain lands north of Mesopotamia (51:11, 27-28).

decisions.choice: a warrior who bereaves: the reading of the text followed here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word, as the text followed here points it, means "one who makes childless", a killer. With a small difference in one letter, as many Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient translations have it, it means "skilled": "a skilled warrior". Both readings say the arrows will do deadly work.

decisions.choice: does not return empty: never misses
decisions.reason: An arrow or a sword that comes back "empty" has struck nothing; one that does not return empty has drawn blood (2 Samuel 1:22). The arrows will all hit their mark.

decisions.choice: its arrows ... he: the army as one warrior
decisions.reason: "Its arrows" belong to the company of nations, spoken of as one; the warrior they are compared to is "he".

decisions.choice: leaves families childless; never come back empty (B); find its mark (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out "who bereaves". Readable explains the picture of the arrow that does not return empty (meaning decision m3).

records.source: וְהָיְתָ֥ה כַשְׂדִּ֖ים לְשָׁלָ֑ל כָּל־שֹׁלְלֶ֥יהָ יִשְׂבָּ֖עוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And will become Chaldea plunder; all plundering her will be satisfied, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Chaldea will be looted; \q all who loot her will have their fill, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.10: And Chaldea will become plunder; \q all who plunder her will be satisfied, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: Babylonia will be robbed. \q Everyone who robs it will take all they want, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Chaldea: the land of the Chaldeans
decisions.reason: The name of the people, "Chaldeans", here stands for their land, as the feminine verb and "her" show (51:24, 35; Ezekiel 23:16).

decisions.choice: plundered in turn
decisions.reason: Babylon had carried off the wealth of Jerusalem (20:5; 52:17-23). Now its own riches will be taken, and those who take them will have all they want.

decisions.choice: Chaldea (B), Babylonia (R); have their fill (B), take all they want (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the land in its familiar form. "Be satisfied" is said in plain words.

records.source: כִּ֤י תִשְׂמְחוּ֙ כִּ֣י תַֽעֲלְז֔וּשֹׁסֵ֖י נַחֲלָתִ֑י כִּ֤י תָפ֨וּשׁוּ֙ כְּעֶגְלָ֣ה דָשָׁ֔ה וְתִצְהֲל֖וּ כָּאֲבִּרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Because you rejoice, because you exult, plunderers of my inheritance, because you frisk like [a] heifer threshing, and you neigh like stallions,
pieces: Because you rejoice and gloat, \q you who plunder {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance, \q because you frisk like a heifer at the threshing \q and neigh like stallions,

L.11: Because you rejoice, because you exult, \q you plunderers of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance, \q because you frisk like a heifer threshing \q and neigh like stallions,

R.11: People of Babylon, you robbed the land that belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and you are glad and celebrate. \q You jump around like a young cow on the threshing floor, \q and you neigh like strong horses.

decisions.choice: you rejoice ... neigh: plural, the reading marked for reading aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has the four verbs as words to one woman, Babylon herself. The reading the scribes marked for reading aloud has them in the plural, spoken to the Babylonians, which fits "plunderers" and "your mother" in verse 12. The reading aloud is followed; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: my inheritance: God's own land and people
decisions.reason: The inheritance is what belongs to God as his own, the land of Israel and its people (2:7; 12:7-9). Babylon plundered it when it took Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a heifer threshing ... stallions: well-fed animals full of high spirits
decisions.reason: Grain was threshed by driving cattle over it, and a heifer at the threshing could eat as she worked (Deuteronomy 25:4; Hosea 10:11), so she was fat and frisky. Stallions neigh in their strength (5:8; 8:16). The pictures mock Babylon's careless glee over its spoils.

decisions.choice: because ...: the reason for the shame in verse 12
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 12, which says what will follow from Babylon's gloating. The word can also mean "though": though they rejoice now, their mother will be put to shame.

decisions.choice: People of Babylon ... the land that belongs to me ... young cow ... strong horses
decisions.reason: Readable names who is spoken to, explains "inheritance", and uses plain words for the animals. It ends its sentences here; verse 12 begins with "So".

records.source: בּ֤וֹשָׁה אִמְּכֶם֙ מְאֹ֔ד חָפְרָ֖ה יֽוֹלַדְתְּכֶ֑ם הִנֵּה֙ אַחֲרִ֣ית גּוֹיִ֔ם מִדְבָּ֖ר צִיָּ֥ה וַעֲרָבָֽה׃
records.gloss: ashamed [is] your mother greatly; disgraced [is] she who bore you; look, [the] last of [the] nations, [a] wilderness, [a] dry land and [a] desert.
pieces: your mother will be deeply ashamed; \q she who gave you birth will be disgraced. \q See, she will be the least of the nations, \q a wilderness, a parched land, a desert.

L.12: your mother will be utterly put to shame; \q she who bore you will be disgraced. \q Look, [she will be] the last of the nations, \q a wilderness, a dry land and a desert.

R.12: So Babylon, your mother, will be deeply ashamed. \q The city that gave birth to you will be disgraced. \q It will become the least important of all nations. \q It will be a dry and empty desert.

decisions.choice: your mother: Babylon herself, whose people are her children
decisions.reason: A city or nation is pictured as the mother of its people (Hosea 2:4; Isaiah 50:1). The shame of Babylon falls on all who belong to her.

decisions.choice: the last of the nations: the lowest, once the first
decisions.reason: The word means the last or hindmost. Babylon, the head of the nations, will be at the bottom of them. Another way to take the phrase is "look, the end of the nations", meaning Babylon's final state; either way, she ends as a desert.

decisions.choice: will be ashamed: the coming shame spoken of as done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for a finished act; as elsewhere in the poem, the certain future is told as if it had happened.

decisions.choice: So Babylon, your mother ... least important ... a dry and empty desert
decisions.reason: Readable says who the mother is (meaning decision m1) and joins the three words for desert land into one phrase.

records.source: מִקֶּ֤צֶף יְהוָה֙ לֹ֣א תֵשֵׁ֔ב וְהָיְתָ֥ה שְׁמָמָ֖ה כֻּלָּ֑הּ כֹּ֚ל עֹבֵ֣ר עַל־בָּבֶ֔ל יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְיִשְׁרֹ֖ק עַל־כָּל־מַכּוֹתֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Because of [the] wrath of Yahweh not she will be inhabited, and she will be [a] desolation, all of her; everyone passing by Babylon will be appalled and will hiss over all her blows.
pieces: Because of the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} no one will live in her; \q she will be wholly desolate. \q Everyone who passes by Babylon \q will be appalled and will hiss in scorn at all her wounds.

L.13: Because of the wrath of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} she will not be inhabited, \q but she will be a desolation, all of her. \q Everyone who passes by Babylon \q will be appalled and will hiss over all her blows.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is angry, so no one will live in Babylon. \q The whole city will be an empty ruin. \q Everyone who passes by \q will be shocked and will make fun of it because of all the disasters that have struck it.

decisions.choice: appalled and hiss: the sound people made at a ruin, in shock and in scorn
decisions.reason: As in 19:8, the hissing or whistling of passers-by was a gesture of horror and of mockery at a ruined place (18:16; 1 Kings 9:8; Lamentations 2:15).

decisions.choice: the words once spoken against Jerusalem, now against Babylon
decisions.reason: The last line repeats 19:8, said of Jerusalem, almost word for word (also 49:17, of Edom). The fate Babylon brought on Jerusalem comes back on Babylon.

decisions.choice: her blows: the wounds she has suffered
decisions.reason: The word means a blow or a wound, and so a disaster that strikes; the city is pictured as a body covered with wounds (19:8).

decisions.choice: will be appalled and will hiss over all her blows (L); hiss in scorn at all her wounds (B); make fun of it because of all the disasters (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of 19:8 at each level, with "her" for Babylon at Literal and Balanced. Readable puts the wrath of the LORD as "the LORD is angry".

records.source: עִרְכ֨וּ עַל־בָּבֶ֤ל׀סָבִיב֙ כָּל־דֹּ֣רְכֵי קֶ֔שֶׁת יְד֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ אַֽל־תַּחְמְל֖וּ אֶל־חֵ֑ץ כִּ֥י לַֽיהוָ֖ה חָטָֽאָה׃
records.gloss: Array [yourselves] against Babylon all around, all bending [the] bow; shoot at her; do not spare [any] arrow, for against Yahweh she has sinned.
pieces: Take up your positions around Babylon, \q all you archers. \q Shoot at her; do not hold back a single arrow, \q for she has sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: Line up against Babylon all around, \q all you who bend the bow; \q shoot at her, do not spare an arrow, \q for she has sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: Surround Babylon and get ready to fight, \q all you soldiers with bows. \q Shoot at the city! Use all your arrows! \q Babylon has sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: all who bend the bow: the archers
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "those who tread the bow": a large bow was strung by bracing it with the foot (46:9; 51:3). It names the archers of the attacking army.

decisions.choice: do not spare an arrow: shoot every one
decisions.reason: To spare something is to hold it back. The archers are to use all they have against the city.

decisions.choice: she has sinned against the LORD: the reason for the attack
decisions.reason: Babylon is judged not only for what it did to other nations but as a sin against God himself: its pride and its cruelty to his people (verses 29, 33; 51:24).

decisions.choice: Take up your positions (B); Surround ... get ready to fight (R); archers (B), soldiers with bows (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to set in battle order. Balanced and Readable say "archers" or "soldiers with bows" for those who bend the bow.

records.source: הָרִ֨יעוּ עָלֶ֤יהָ סָבִיב֙ נָתְנָ֣ה יָדָ֔הּ נָֽפְלוּ֙ אָשְׁיוֹתֶ֔יהָ נֶהֶרְס֖וּ חֽוֹמוֹתֶ֑יהָ כִּי֩ נִקְמַ֨ת יְהוָ֥ה הִיא֙ הִנָּ֣קְמוּ בָ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה עֲשׂוּ־לָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Raise [a] shout against her all around; she has given her hand; have fallen her towers; are torn down her walls; for [the] vengeance of Yahweh it [is]; take vengeance on her; as she has done, do to her.
pieces: Shout the battle cry against her on every side! She has surrendered; \q her towers have fallen, \q her walls are torn down. \q This is the vengeance of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Take vengeance on her; \q do to her as she has done.

L.15: Raise a war cry against her all around; she has given her hand. \q Her towers have fallen, \q her walls are torn down. \q For this is the vengeance of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: take vengeance on her; \q as she has done, do to her.

R.15: Shout the war cry all around the city! Babylon has given up. \q Its towers have fallen, \q and its walls have been torn down. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is paying Babylon back. So pay it back! \q Do to it what it did to others.

decisions.choice: she has given her hand: she has surrendered
decisions.reason: To give one's hand is to pledge oneself to another, and so to submit to him (1 Chronicles 29:24; 2 Chronicles 30:8; Lamentations 5:6). The city gives in to its attackers.

decisions.choice: her towers: a rare word for part of the city's defenses
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It may mean towers, buttresses or foundations of the walls; the written text and the reading the scribes marked for reading aloud spell it slightly differently. The line beside it, "her walls are torn down", shows that it names her defenses.

decisions.choice: the vengeance of the LORD: just repayment, not blind revenge
decisions.reason: God's vengeance in Jeremiah is the act of the judge who puts right a wrong and repays the guilty (11:20; 51:6, 11). Babylon will get what it gave: "as she has done, do to her" (verse 29; Psalm 137:8). The attackers carry out the sentence.

decisions.choice: is paying Babylon back. So pay it back! ... what it did to others
decisions.reason: Readable says "pay back" for taking vengeance (meaning decision m3) and names whom Babylon wronged.

records.source: כִּרְת֤וּ זוֹרֵ֨עַ֙ מִבָּבֶ֔ל וְתֹפֵ֥שׂ מַגָּ֖ל בְּעֵ֣ת קָצִ֑יר מִפְּנֵי֙ חֶ֣רֶב הַיּוֹנָ֔ה אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־עַמּוֹ֙ יִפְנ֔וּ וְאִ֥ישׁ לְאַרְצ֖וֹ יָנֻֽסוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Cut off [the] sower from Babylon and [the] one wielding [the] sickle in [the] time of harvest; from before [the] sword of the oppressor each to his people they will turn, and each to his land they will flee.
pieces: Cut off from Babylon the one who sows \q and the one who swings the sickle at harvest. \q Before the oppressor's sword \q everyone will turn back to their own people; \q everyone will flee to their own land.

L.16: Cut off the sower from Babylon, \q and the one who handles the sickle at harvest time. \q Before the sword of the oppressor \q each will turn to {{gender:their|his}} own people, \q and each will flee to {{gender:their|his}} own land.

R.16: Destroy everyone in Babylon who plants seed \q or cuts the grain at harvest time. \q Because of the cruel enemy's sword, \q all the foreigners will go back to their own people. \q They will run away to their own countries.

decisions.choice: the sower ... the one with the sickle: the farmers whose fields fed the city
decisions.reason: Babylon was surrounded by farmland watered by canals. With the sowers and reapers gone, no food will be grown or gathered; the land will become the desert of verse 12.

decisions.choice: the sword of the oppressor: the sword of the cruel enemy
decisions.reason: The word means one who oppresses or acts with violence, as in 25:38 and 46:16. It is spelled like the word for "dove", but "oppressor" fits the sword.

decisions.choice: each will turn to their own people: the foreigners in Babylon go home
decisions.reason: Babylon was full of people from many nations, brought there as traders, workers and captives (verse 37; 51:9, 44). When the city falls they will scatter to their own lands (Isaiah 13:14).

decisions.choice: Destroy everyone ... the cruel enemy's sword ... all the foreigners
decisions.reason: Readable says what "cut off" means, explains "the oppressor", and names the foreigners as those who flee (meaning decision m3).

records.source: שֶׂ֧ה פְזוּרָ֛ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲרָי֣וֹת הִדִּ֑יחוּ הָרִאשׁ֤וֹן אֲכָלוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְזֶ֤ה הָאַחֲרוֹן֙ עִצְּמ֔וֹ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃ס
records.gloss: [A] sheep scattered [is] Israel; lions have driven [him] away; the first devoured him, [the] king of Assyria, and this the last has gnawed his bones, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
pieces: Israel is a stray sheep chased off by lions. \q First the king of Assyria devoured him; \q now, last of all, he has had his bones gnawed \q by Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.

L.17: Israel is a scattered sheep; lions have driven him away. \q The first who devoured him was the king of Assyria, \q and this last one has gnawed his bones, \q Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.

R.17: The people of Israel are like a sheep that lions have chased away from the flock. \q First the king of Assyria ate them up. \q Last of all, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon \q has chewed up their bones.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria ... Nebuchadrezzar: the two empires that destroyed Israel and Judah
decisions.reason: Assyria conquered the northern kingdom of Israel and took its people into exile in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:6). Nebuchadrezzar of Babylon destroyed Jerusalem and took Judah into exile in 587 BC (2 Kings 25). Israel here means the whole people.

decisions.choice: gnawed his bones: finished off what was left
decisions.reason: The verb is made from the word for "bone" and is found only here: to break or crunch the bones. After the first lion ate the flesh, the second left nothing.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the form of the name used here
decisions.reason: Jeremiah usually spells the name Nebuchadrezzar, closer to its Babylonian form, Nabu-kudurri-usur (21:2; 25:9); in some chapters it is Nebuchadnezzar (27:6). Both name the same king.

decisions.choice: a scattered sheep driven off by lions
decisions.reason: The flock of verse 6 is pictured again: a single sheep cut off from the flock, at the mercy of beasts of prey. The kings who attacked it are the lions.

decisions.choice: he has had his bones gnawed by Nebuchadrezzar (B); the people of Israel ... them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the order of "first" and "last". Readable speaks of the people of Israel as "them", since the one sheep stands for the whole people, and says "like" to show the picture.

records.heading: Israel brought home

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֥י פֹקֵ֛ד אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְאֶל־אַרְצ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּקַ֖דְתִּי אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: look, I [am] punishing [the] king of Babylon and his land, as I punished [the] king of Assyria.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: \q I will bring punishment on the king of Babylon and on his land, \q as I did to the king of Assyria.

L.18: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: \q Look, I am going to punish the king of Babylon and his land, \q just as I punished the king of Assyria.

R.18: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: \q I am going to punish the king of Babylon and his country, \q just as I punished the king of Assyria.

decisions.choice: punish: visit with judgment
decisions.reason: The verb means to visit, to call to account, and so to punish (25:12; 46:25). The "look" with the verb in this form means God is about to act.

decisions.choice: as I punished the king of Assyria: Assyria's fall
decisions.reason: Assyria's capital, Nineveh, fell in 612 BC to the Babylonians and the Medes (Nahum 2-3), and the empire ended a few years later. The power that destroyed Assyria will now be judged in the same way.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies ... says this (B); This is what the LORD of Armies says (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for the messenger formula and for the LORD of hosts, as in Isaiah.

records.source: וְשֹׁבַבְתִּ֤י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־נָוֵ֔הוּ וְרָעָ֥ה הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל וְהַבָּשָׁ֑ן וּבְהַ֥ר אֶפְרַ֛יִם וְהַגִּלְעָ֖ד תִּשְׂבַּ֥ע נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I will bring back Israel to his pasture, and he will graze [on] Carmel and Bashan, and on [the] hill country of Ephraim and Gilead will be satisfied his appetite.
pieces: I will bring Israel back to his own pasture, \q and he will graze on Carmel and in Bashan; \q in the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead he will eat his fill.

L.19: And I will bring Israel back to his pasture, \q and he will graze on Carmel and on Bashan, \q and on the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead his appetite will be satisfied.

R.19: But I will bring the people of Israel back to their own land, like sheep to their pasture. \q They will eat on Mount Carmel and in Bashan. \q They will eat all they want in the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.

decisions.choice: Carmel, Bashan, Ephraim, Gilead: the richest grazing land of the north
decisions.reason: Carmel is the wooded ridge by the sea; Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee, was famous for its cattle (Amos 4:1); the hill country of Ephraim is the heart of the old northern kingdom; Gilead lies east of the Jordan. These were among the first lands lost to Assyria (2 Kings 15:29), and they are promised back.

decisions.choice: Bashan and Gilead: as in Micah's prayer
decisions.reason: Micah prays that God will shepherd his flock "in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old" (Micah 7:14). The same hope is given here.

decisions.choice: his appetite will be satisfied: he will eat his fill
decisions.reason: The word often translated "soul" here means desire or appetite, the hunger of the sheep (31:14, 25). The flock that was devoured (verse 17) will itself be well fed.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel ... their own land, like sheep to their pasture ... Mount Carmel
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the sheep and its pasture and speaks of Israel as "them", as in verse 17.

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵם֩ וּבָעֵ֨ת הַהִ֜יא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה יְבֻקַּ֞שׁ אֶת־עֲוֺ֤ן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאֵינֶ֔נּוּ וְאֶת־חַטֹּ֥את יְהוּדָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תִמָּצֶ֑אינָה כִּ֥י אֶסְלַ֖ח לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אַשְׁאִֽיר׃
records.gloss: In the days those and in the time that, declares Yahweh, will be sought [the] iniquity of Israel, and there [will be] none, and [the] sins of Judah, and not they will be found, for I will pardon whom I leave as [a] remnant.
pieces: In those days, at that time, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the guilt of Israel will be searched for, but there will be none; \q the sins of Judah, but they will not be found; \q for I will forgive those I leave alive.

L.20: In those days and at that time, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the iniquity of Israel will be sought, and there will be none, \q and the sins of Judah, and they will not be found; \q for I will pardon those whom I leave as a remnant.

R.20: When that time comes, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, people will look for Israel's sin, but there will not be any. \q They will look for Judah's sins, but they will not find any, \q because I will forgive the people I let survive.

decisions.choice: sought and not found: forgiveness that removes sin entirely
decisions.reason: No one searching will find the people's sin, because God has forgiven it (31:34; 33:8; Micah 7:18-19). The words echo the promise of the new covenant, "I will remember their sin no more".

decisions.choice: those whom I leave: the remnant who survive
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave over, to let survive. The remnant is the people God has kept through the judgment (23:3; 31:7).

decisions.choice: iniquity (L), guilt (B), sin (R); pardon (L), forgive (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the word for iniquity. Balanced and Readable say "forgive" for the verb, which is used only of God's forgiving.

decisions.choice: people will look for ... they will not find
decisions.reason: Readable makes the passive verbs active with "people" as the subject, and joins the two phrases for the time, as in verse 4.

records.source: עַל־הָאָ֤רֶץ מְרָתַ֨יִם֙ עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ וְאֶל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י פְּק֑וֹד חֲרֹ֨ב וְהַחֲרֵ֤ם אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וַעֲשֵׂ֕ה כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִֽיךָ׃ס
records.gloss: Against the land of Merathaim, go up against her, and against [the] inhabitants of Pekod; kill and devote [them to destruction] after them, declares Yahweh, and do according to all that I have commanded you.
pieces: Go up against the land of Merathaim, \q and against those who live in Pekod. \q Kill them and devote them to destruction to the very last, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q do everything I have commanded you.

L.21: Against the land of Merathaim, go up against it, \q and against the inhabitants of Pekod. \q Kill and devote them to destruction to the last, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and do according to all that I have commanded you.

R.21: Attack Merathaim, the land of double rebellion! \q Attack the people who live in Pekod, the place of punishment! \q Kill them, and destroy every one of them completely, as given over to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Do everything I have told you to do.

decisions.choice: Merathaim and Pekod: real names turned into wordplay
decisions.reason: Merathaim means "double rebellion" (or "double bitterness"), and Pekod sounds like the word for "punishment" or "visitation" (as in verses 18, 27 and 31). Both seem to play on real names: Babylonian texts call the marshy land at the head of the Persian Gulf "the land of the Bitter River" (mat marrati), and the Puqudu were an Aramean people living east of Babylon, named as Pekod in Ezekiel 23:23. So Babylon is called the land of double rebellion and the people of punishment.

decisions.choice: devote them to destruction: the ban of holy war
decisions.reason: To devote something to destruction was to give it over wholly to God, so that nothing was kept back for one's own use (Deuteronomy 7:2; Joshua 6:17). God once used Babylon to do this to Judah (25:9); now Babylon is put under the ban. "After them" means pursuing them to the last.

decisions.choice: go up ... do ...: commands to one attacker
decisions.reason: The commands are singular: God speaks to the leader of the attacking army, or to the army as one. "All that I have commanded you" shows that the attacker carries out God's orders (verse 25; Isaiah 13:3-5).

decisions.choice: devote ... to destruction (L, B); destroy ... completely, as given over to me (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the ban; Readable explains it, as the terms list says.

decisions.choice: the land of double rebellion ... the place of punishment
decisions.reason: Readable adds the meaning of each name, so that the reader can hear the wordplay (meaning decision m1). The meanings are added beside the names, not in place of them.

records.source: ק֥וֹל מִלְחָמָ֖ה בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְשֶׁ֖בֶר גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: [A] sound of battle in the land, and destruction great.
pieces: The noise of battle is in the land, \q and great destruction!

L.22: A sound of battle in the land, \q and great destruction!

R.22: Listen! The noise of battle is in the land. \q Everything is being destroyed.

decisions.choice: great destruction: the cry once raised over Judah
decisions.reason: "Great destruction" was the alarm over Judah (4:6; 6:1) and over Moab (48:3). Now it is heard in Babylon.

decisions.choice: a sound of battle: an exclamation
decisions.reason: The line has no verb. It is a cry, as if the hearer is called to listen to the battle already raging.

decisions.choice: Listen! ... Everything is being destroyed.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the cry into short sentences and says what "great destruction" means.

records.source: אֵ֤יךְ נִגְדַּע֙ וַיִּשָּׁבֵ֔ר פַּטִּ֖ישׁ כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֣יךְ הָיְתָ֧ה לְשַׁמָּ֛ה בָּבֶ֖ל בַּגּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: How has been cut down and broken [the] hammer of all the earth! How has become [a] horror Babylon among the nations!
pieces: How the hammer of the whole earth \q is cut down and shattered! \q How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!

L.23: How the hammer of the whole earth \q has been cut down and broken! \q How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!

R.23: Babylon was like a hammer that beat down the whole earth, \q but now it has been cut down and broken! \q The nations are horrified at what has happened to Babylon!

decisions.choice: the hammer of the whole earth: the power that smashed the nations
decisions.reason: Babylon is pictured as a smith's hammer that broke every nation it struck. In 51:20-23 God calls it his war club, with which he shattered nations. Now the hammer itself is broken.

decisions.choice: How ...!: a cry of lament and of wonder
decisions.reason: The word begins laments (Lamentations 1:1; 2 Samuel 1:19) and mocking songs over fallen tyrants (Isaiah 14:4, 12). Here it mourns, with irony, Babylon's fall.

decisions.choice: a horror: a ruin that stuns all who see it
decisions.reason: As in 25:11 and verse 13, the word means a desolation and the horror it causes.

decisions.choice: was like a hammer that beat down ... The nations are horrified
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hammer and says the cry over Babylon in plain words.

records.source: יָקֹ֨שְׁתִּי לָ֤ךְ וְגַם־נִלְכַּדְתְּ֙ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאַ֖תְּ לֹ֣א יָדָ֑עַתְּ נִמְצֵאת֙ וְגַם־נִתְפַּ֔שְׂתְּ כִּ֥י בַֽיהוָ֖ה הִתְגָּרִֽית׃
records.gloss: I laid [a] snare for you, and also you were caught, Babylon, and you not knew; you were found and also seized, for against Yahweh you strove.
pieces: I laid a trap for you, Babylon, and it caught you \q before you were aware of it. \q You were found out and seized, \q because you fought against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.24: I set a snare for you, and you were caught, Babylon, \q and you did not know it; \q you were found and also seized, \q because you contended against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.24: Babylon, I set a trap for you, \q and you were caught before you knew what was happening. \q You were found and captured, \q because you fought against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I set a snare: God himself traps Babylon
decisions.reason: The hunter's snare is a picture of sudden capture (5:26; Lamentations 3:52). God speaks: the city did not fall by chance, and it was taken by surprise. Babylon fell in 539 BC without a long siege.

decisions.choice: you contended against the LORD: you challenged him
decisions.reason: The verb means to stir up strife, to pick a fight (Deuteronomy 2:5, 9). By its pride and its treatment of God's people, Babylon made itself God's opponent (verse 29).

decisions.choice: you were caught ... found ... seized: past tense of what is certain
decisions.reason: As in verses 2-3, the verbs speak of the capture as already done.

decisions.choice: Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the name next to "you" and join "you did not know it" to the capture.

records.source: פָּתַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת־א֣וֹצָר֔וֹ וַיּוֹצֵ֖א אֶת־כְּלֵ֣י זַעְמ֑וֹ כִּי־מְלָאכָ֣ה הִ֗יא לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Has opened Yahweh his armory, and has brought out [the] weapons of his indignation, for [a] work it [is] of [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts in [the] land of [the] Chaldeans.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has opened {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} armory \q and brought out the weapons of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath, \q for the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.

L.25: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has opened {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} armory \q and has brought out the weapons of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} indignation, \q for this is a work of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts in the land of the Chaldeans.

R.25: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has opened the room where {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} weapons are kept. \q He has brought out the weapons {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} uses when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is angry. \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies has work to do in the land of the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: his armory ... the weapons of his indignation: the nations God uses to punish
decisions.reason: The word means a storehouse; here it holds weapons. The same phrase, "the weapons of his indignation", names the armies God gathers against Babylon in Isaiah 13:5. The weapons are the attacking nations.

decisions.choice: a work: a task God has to carry out
decisions.reason: The word is used of work to be done (48:10). The judgment of Babylon is God's own work, which he will finish.

decisions.choice: the Lord GOD of hosts: the master of every army
decisions.reason: The title joins "Lord" with the divine name and "of hosts" (2:19). The armies at Babylon's gates come because the commander of all armies has sent them.

decisions.choice: the Lord GOD of hosts (L), of Armies (B, R); Chaldeans (L, B), Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these titles and names. Readable explains "armory" and "weapons of indignation".

records.source: בֹּֽאוּ־לָ֤הּ מִקֵּץ֙ פִּתְח֣וּ מַאֲבֻסֶ֔יהָ סָלּ֥וּהָ כְמוֹ־עֲרֵמִ֖ים וְהַחֲרִימ֑וּהָ אַל־תְּהִי־לָ֖הּ שְׁאֵרִֽית׃
records.gloss: Come against her from [the] end; open her granaries; pile her up like heaps, and devote her [to destruction]; not let there be for her [a] remnant.
pieces: Come against her from the farthest places; break open her storehouses; \q pile her up like heaps of grain and devote her to destruction. \q Leave nothing of her.

L.26: Come against her from every border; open her granaries; \q pile her up like heaps of grain and devote her to destruction; \q let nothing be left of her.

R.26: Come and attack Babylon from far away. Break open its storehouses. \q Pile everything up like heaps of grain, and destroy it completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Do not let anything be left.

decisions.choice: from the end: from every border, from the farthest places
decisions.reason: "From the end" can mean from the far ends of the earth (verse 41) or from every side of the city (51:31). Either way, the attackers are to come from everywhere at once.

decisions.choice: granaries ... heaps: her stores of grain, and the heaps that she will become
decisions.reason: The word for "granaries" is used only here; it comes from a word for feeding animals, and so means storehouses of grain. The heaps are heaps of grain, as on a threshing floor (Ruth 3:7), and also perhaps the heaps of rubble a ruined city becomes (Nehemiah 3:34).

decisions.choice: devote her to destruction: as in verse 21
decisions.reason: Everything is to be given over wholly to God, and nothing kept back (Joshua 6:17).

decisions.choice: destroy it completely, as given over to the LORD; from far away
decisions.reason: The settled Readable wording for the ban, as in verse 21.

records.source: חִרְבוּ֙ כָּל־פָּרֶ֔יהָ יֵרְד֖וּ לַטָּ֑בַח ה֣וֹי עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־בָ֥א יוֹמָ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: Kill all her young bulls; let them go down to the slaughter; woe on them, for has come their day, [the] time of their punishment.
pieces: Kill all her young bulls; \q let them go down to be slaughtered. \q Woe to them, \q for their day has arrived, the time for them to be punished.

L.27: Kill all her young bulls; \q let them go down to the slaughter. \q Woe on them, \q for their day has come, the time of their punishment.

R.27: Kill all of Babylon's young soldiers, strong as young bulls. \q Let them be slaughtered like animals. \q How terrible it will be for them! \q The time has come for them to be punished.

decisions.choice: her young bulls: her strong young warriors
decisions.reason: Young bulls are a picture of strong fighting men and leaders (46:21; Isaiah 34:7; Psalm 22:13). They will be led to slaughter as animals are.

decisions.choice: their day, the time of their punishment: the day God has set to judge them
decisions.reason: The word for "punishment" is the noun of the verb "visit" (verse 18): the time when God calls them to account (46:21; 48:44).

decisions.choice: Woe on them (L); Woe to them (B); How terrible it will be for them (R)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for the cry of woe, as in Isaiah. Readable explains the young bulls as soldiers (meaning decision m1).

records.source: ק֥וֹל נָסִ֛ים וּפְלֵטִ֖ים מֵאֶ֣רֶץ בָּבֶ֑ל לְהַגִּ֣יד בְּצִיּ֗וֹן אֶת־נִקְמַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ נִקְמַ֖ת הֵיכָלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [The] sound of fugitives and escapees from [the] land of Babylon, to declare in Zion [the] vengeance of Yahweh our God, [the] vengeance of his temple.
pieces: Listen! Fugitives and refugees are coming from the land of Babylon \q to tell in Zion of the vengeance of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, \q vengeance for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple.

L.28: The sound of those who flee and escape from the land of Babylon, \q to declare in Zion the vengeance of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, \q the vengeance for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple!

R.28: Listen! People are escaping from Babylon. \q They are running to Zion to tell how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has paid Babylon back. \q He has paid it back for destroying {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple.

decisions.choice: the sound of: Listen!
decisions.reason: The word "sound" or "voice" at the start of a line is often a cry to listen (3:21; 4:15; verse 22).

decisions.choice: fugitives ... our God: God's people escaping home
decisions.reason: Those who flee are the exiles of verse 8, getting away as Babylon falls. They bring the news to Zion, and the words "our God" are theirs.

decisions.choice: vengeance for his temple: repayment for its destruction
decisions.reason: Babylon burned the temple in Jerusalem (52:13) and carried off its treasures (52:17-23). Its fall is God's answer to that crime (51:11).

decisions.choice: paid Babylon back ... for destroying his temple
decisions.reason: Readable says "paid back" for vengeance (verse 15) and says what was done to the temple.

records.source: הַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ אֶל־בָּבֶ֣ל׀רַ֠בִּים כָּל־דֹּ֨רְכֵי קֶ֜שֶׁת חֲנ֧וּ עָלֶ֣יהָ סָבִ֗יב אַל־יְהִי־לָהּ֙פְּלֵטָ֔ה שַׁלְּמוּ־לָ֣הּ כְּפָעֳלָ֔הּ כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה עֲשׂוּ־לָ֑הּ כִּ֧י אֶל־יְהוָ֛ה זָ֖דָה אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Summon against Babylon archers, all bending [the] bow; encamp against her all around; not let there be for her escape; repay her according to her deed[s]; according to all that she has done, do to her; for against Yahweh she has been arrogant, against [the] Holy One of Israel.
pieces: Call up archers against Babylon, all who draw the bow. Camp all around her; let no one escape. \q Pay her back for what she has done; \q do to her just as she has done, \q for she has defied {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in her pride, the Holy One of Israel.

L.29: Summon archers against Babylon, all who bend the bow; encamp against her all around; let there be no escape for her. \q Repay her according to her deeds; \q do to her according to all that she has done, \q for she has acted arrogantly against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, against the Holy One of Israel.

R.29: Call for soldiers with bows to attack Babylon. Put your camps all around the city. Do not let anyone escape. \q Pay Babylon back for what it has done. \q Do to it what it did to others. \q It was proud and defied {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Holy One of Israel.

decisions.choice: archers
decisions.reason: The word usually means "many", but here it is taken from a verb meaning "to shoot" (Job 16:13), as the next words, "all who bend the bow", show. Some read "summon many against Babylon".

decisions.choice: she has acted arrogantly: pride that defies God
decisions.reason: The verb means to act with insolence, to set oneself up against God (Exodus 18:11; Deuteronomy 18:22). Babylon's pride is the charge on which it is judged; verses 31-32 call it "Arrogance" by name.

decisions.choice: the Holy One of Israel: Isaiah's title for God
decisions.reason: The title is found often in Isaiah (1:4; 47:4) but in Jeremiah only here and in 51:5. God is holy, wholly other and pure, and he has bound himself to Israel; to defy him is to defy Israel's God.

decisions.choice: repay her ... do to her: as in verse 15
decisions.reason: The demand that Babylon be paid back for what it did is repeated (verse 15; 51:24; Psalm 137:8).

decisions.choice: defied ... in her pride (B); was proud and defied (R); soldiers with bows (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the arrogance as defiance. Readable names the archers as in verse 14.

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן יִפְּל֥וּ בַחוּרֶ֖יהָ בִּרְחֹבֹתֶ֑יהָ וְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֨י מִלְחַמְתָּ֥הּ יִדַּ֛מּוּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore will fall her young men in her squares, and all her men of war will be silenced in the day that, declares Yahweh.
pieces: So her young men will fall in her streets, \q and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.30: Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, \q and all her men of war will be silenced in that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.30: So Babylon's young men will be killed in the city squares. \q All its soldiers will die on that day, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: repeats 49:26
decisions.reason: The verse repeats, almost word for word, what is said of Damascus in 49:26. The same end comes to Babylon.

decisions.choice: will be silenced: will fall silent in death
decisions.reason: The verb means to be silent, and so to be struck dumb or to perish (8:14; 25:37; 48:2).

decisions.choice: her squares: the open places of the city
decisions.reason: The word means the broad open spaces inside the city gates, where people met and markets were held (5:1; 9:20).

decisions.choice: soldiers (B, R); will die (R)
decisions.reason: "Men of war" means soldiers. Readable says plainly what "silenced" means here (meaning decision m2).

records.source: הִנְנִ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ זָד֔וֹן נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת כִּ֛י בָּ֥א יוֹמְךָ֖ עֵ֥ת פְּקַדְתִּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Look, I [am] against you, Arrogance, declares [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts, for has come your day, [the] time [that] I will punish you.
pieces: I am against you, Arrogant One, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q for your day has arrived, the time for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to punish you.

L.31: Look, I am against you, Arrogance, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q for your day has come, the time that I will punish you.

R.31: Listen, you proud city! I am your enemy, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q Your day has come, the time for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to punish you.

decisions.choice: Arrogance: pride used as a name for Babylon
decisions.reason: The word means pride, insolence (49:16). Here and in verse 32 it stands where a name stands, as God calls Babylon by its chief sin: "Arrogance", or "Proud One". Egypt is named in the same way "Rahab" in Isaiah 30:7.

decisions.choice: I am against you: I am your enemy
decisions.reason: This is a formula of open hostility, God declaring war on a city or people (21:13; 51:25; Nahum 2:14).

decisions.choice: your day, the time that I will punish you
decisions.reason: As in verse 27, the day is the time God has set to call Babylon to account.

decisions.choice: Arrogance (L); Arrogant One (B); you proud city (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the noun as a name. Balanced makes it a title for a person, and Readable says plainly whom God addresses. All three take it as a name for Babylon (meaning decision m1).

records.source: וְכָשַׁ֤ל זָדוֹן֙ וְנָפַ֔ל וְאֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ מֵקִ֑ים וְהִצַּ֤תִּי אֵשׁ֙ בְּעָרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֖ה כָּל־סְבִיבֹתָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: And will stumble Arrogance and fall, and there [is] none for him raising [him] up; and I will kindle fire in his cities, and it will devour all around him.
pieces: The Arrogant One will stumble and fall, \q and no one will lift him up. \q I will set fire to his towns, \q and it will consume everything around him.

L.32: And Arrogance will stumble and fall, \q with no one to raise him up; \q and I will kindle a fire in his cities, \q and it will devour all that is around him.

R.32: The proud city will trip and fall, \q and no one will help it get up. \q I will set its towns on fire, \q and the fire will burn up everything around it.

decisions.choice: him, his: Babylon spoken of by its name "Arrogance"
decisions.reason: The name is a masculine word, so Babylon, usually "she" in this chapter, is here "he". The person meant is still the city and its empire, perhaps with its king.

decisions.choice: fire that devours all around: as in 21:14
decisions.reason: God threatened Jerusalem in the same words (21:14; compare 17:27; 49:27). "No one to raise him up" echoes the lament over Israel in Amos 5:2.

decisions.choice: The proud city ... it
decisions.reason: Readable names the city as in verse 31 and calls it "it".

records.source: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת עֲשׁוּקִ֛ים בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל וּבְנֵי־יְהוּדָ֖ה יַחְדָּ֑ו וְכָל־שֹֽׁבֵיהֶם֙ הֶחֱזִ֣יקוּ בָ֔ם מֵאֲנ֖וּ שַׁלְּחָֽם׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: oppressed [are the] sons of Israel and [the] sons of Judah together, and all their captors have held fast to them; they have refused to let them go.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are oppressed, and the {{gender:people of Judah|sons of Judah}} as well. \q All their captors hold them tight \q and refuse to let them go.

L.33: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q The {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel are oppressed, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah with them; \q all who took them captive have held them fast; \q they have refused to let them go.

R.33: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the {{gender:people of Judah|sons of Judah}} are both being treated cruelly. \q The people who captured them hold on to them \q and will not let them go.

decisions.choice: they refused to let them go: like Pharaoh in Egypt
decisions.reason: The words recall Pharaoh, who refused to let Israel go (Exodus 4:23; 7:14; 9:2). Babylon plays the part of Egypt, and the return from exile is a new exodus (16:14-15; 23:7-8).

decisions.choice: Israel and Judah together: both peoples in exile, both to be freed
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, the northern and southern peoples are named together. Both were taken captive, by Assyria and by Babylon, and both are under God's care.

decisions.choice: children of Israel (L); Israelites (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for "sons of Israel", with the traditional form as the alternative; "sons of Judah" follows it. The messenger formula is the book's settled wording.

records.heading: The strong Redeemer

records.source: גֹּאֲלָ֣ם׀חָזָ֗ק יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שְׁמ֔וֹ רִ֥יב יָרִ֖יב אֶת־רִיבָ֑ם לְמַ֨עַן֙ הִרְגִּ֣יעַ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִרְגִּ֖יז לְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃
records.gloss: Their Redeemer [is] strong; Yahweh of hosts [is] his name; surely he will plead their case, so as to give rest to the earth and to give unrest to [the] inhabitants of Babylon.
pieces: Their Redeemer is strong; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. \q He will take up their case and win it, \q so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may bring rest to the earth \q and turmoil to those who live in Babylon.

L.34: Their Redeemer is strong; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. \q He will surely plead their case, \q so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may give rest to the earth \q and give unrest to the inhabitants of Babylon.

R.34: But the one who rescues them is strong. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. \q He will stand up for them and win their case. \q He will give rest to the earth, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring trouble on the people of Babylon.

decisions.choice: their Redeemer: the next of kin who buys back and defends
decisions.reason: A redeemer was the relative who bought back a family member sold into slavery and stood up for him (Leviticus 25:47-49; Ruth 4). God takes that part for his captive people: their captors will not let them go (verse 33), but their Redeemer is stronger. The words echo Isaiah 47:4, "Our Redeemer, the LORD of hosts is his name".

decisions.choice: he will surely plead their case: he will act as their defender in court
decisions.reason: The doubled verb makes it certain. God is pictured as the advocate who takes up the case of the helpless and wins it (51:36; Micah 7:9). Proverbs 23:10-11 uses almost the same words of the orphan's strong Redeemer.

decisions.choice: rest ... unrest: a play on two words that sound alike
decisions.reason: The two verbs sound alike and mean opposite things: to give rest and to make tremble. The earth, crushed by Babylon, will have rest; Babylon will have none.

decisions.choice: the one who rescues them
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Redeemer", as the settled wording allows, and makes the court picture plain.

records.source: חֶ֥רֶב עַל־כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל וְאֶל־שָׂרֶ֖יהָ וְאֶל־חֲכָמֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: [A] sword against [the] Chaldeans, declares Yahweh, and against [the] inhabitants of Babylon, and against her princes, and against her wise [men].
pieces: A sword against the Chaldeans, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q against the people of Babylon, \q against her officials and her wise men!

L.35: A sword against the Chaldeans, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and against the inhabitants of Babylon, \q and against her princes and against her wise men!

R.35: A sword will strike the Babylonians, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q It will strike the people who live in Babylon, \q its leaders and its wise men.

decisions.choice: A sword against ...: a chant of judgment
decisions.reason: The word "sword" begins five lines in verses 35-37, each naming a part of Babylon's strength, and a sixth line (verse 38) plays on it. The lines have no verb: they are a war chant, as in Ezekiel 21:14-15.

decisions.choice: her wise men: the scholars and advisers of the court
decisions.reason: Babylon was famous for its learned men, who read omens, the stars and dreams and gave counsel to the king (51:57; Isaiah 47:13; Daniel 2:2). Their wisdom will not save the city.

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); Chaldeans (L, B), Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these words. Readable adds the verb "strike" to the chant and repeats it.

records.source: חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־הַבַּדִּ֖ים וְנֹאָ֑לוּ חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־גִּבּוֹרֶ֖יהָ וָחָֽתּוּ׃
records.gloss: [A] sword against the empty talkers, and they will become fools; [a] sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered.
pieces: A sword against the babblers, so that they become fools! \q A sword against her warriors, so that they are shattered!

L.36: A sword against the empty talkers, and they will become fools! \q A sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered!

R.36: A sword will strike the false prophets, and they will look like fools. \q A sword will strike its soldiers, and they will be broken and terrified.

decisions.choice: the empty talkers: those who speak lies as omens
decisions.reason: The word means idle talk, and so those who talk it: here the diviners and omen-readers of Babylon, as in Isaiah 44:25. Their predictions will be shown to be empty.

decisions.choice: they will become fools: they will be shown up as foolish
decisions.reason: The verb means to be or to act foolishly (5:4; Isaiah 19:13). Events will prove that their words had no meaning.

decisions.choice: shattered: broken and in terror
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the verb means both to be shattered and to be broken by fear.

decisions.choice: empty talkers (L), babblers (B), false prophets (R); broken and terrified (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of Isaiah 44:25 for the same word. Readable gives both sides of the verb "shattered" (meaning decision m3).

records.source: חֶ֜רֶב אֶל־סוּסָ֣יו וְאֶל־רִכְבּ֗וֹ וְאֶל־כָּל־הָעֶ֛רֶב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּתוֹכָ֖הּ וְהָי֣וּ לְנָשִׁ֑ים חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־אוֹצְרֹתֶ֖יהָ וּבֻזָּֽזוּ׃
records.gloss: [A] sword against her horses and against her chariots and against all the mixed people who [are] in her midst, and they will become women; [a] sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered.
pieces: A sword against her horses and her chariots and against all the mixed peoples in her midst, so that they become like women! \q A sword against her treasures, so that they are looted!

L.37: A sword against her horses and against her chariots, and against all the mixed people who are in her midst, and they will become women! \q A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered!

R.37: A sword will strike its horses and its chariots and all the foreigners in the city. They will lose their courage and be afraid. \q A sword will strike its treasures, and they will be carried away.

decisions.choice: the mixed people: foreigners living in Babylon, perhaps hired soldiers
decisions.reason: The word names people of many origins living among a nation (25:20, 24; Exodus 12:38). In Babylon they may be the foreign troops who fought for the city, as the horses and chariots before them suggest, or the foreign residents of verse 16.

decisions.choice: they will become women: they will lose all courage
decisions.reason: In the speech of the time, to say that soldiers become women was to say that they lose heart and cannot fight (51:30; Isaiah 19:16; Nahum 3:13). It describes their terror, not the worth of women.

decisions.choice: her treasures: the same word as "armory" in verse 25
decisions.reason: The word means a storehouse or treasury. God opens his own storehouse of weapons (verse 25), and Babylon's storehouses are plundered.

decisions.choice: like women (B); They will lose their courage and be afraid (R); foreigners (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "like women", since the picture is a comparison. Readable says what it means (meaning decision m2) and uses a plain word for the mixed people.

records.source: חֹ֥רֶב אֶל־מֵימֶ֖יהָ וְיָבֵ֑שׁוּ כִּ֣י אֶ֤רֶץ פְּסִלִים֙ הִ֔יא וּבָאֵימִ֖ים יִתְהֹלָֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: [A] drought against her waters, and they will dry up; for [a] land of carved images it [is], and over [the] terrors they act madly.
pieces: A drought on her waters, so that they dry up! \q For it is a land of idols, \q and they are crazed by their dreadful images.

L.38: A drought against her waters, and they will dry up! \q For it is a land of carved images, \q and they go mad over terrors.

R.38: A drought will come on its waters, and they will dry up. \q For Babylon is a land full of idols, \q and its people have gone crazy over these frightening statues.

decisions.choice: a drought: a play on "sword"
decisions.reason: The word for drought is written with the same letters as the word for sword in verses 35-37; only the vowels differ. With the vowels of the text, the chant ends with a wordplay: after five swords, a drought. Some read the same letters as "sword" here too, continuing the series. The vowels of the text are followed.

decisions.choice: her waters: the Euphrates and the canals
decisions.reason: Babylon stood on the Euphrates, and its fields and its defenses depended on the river and a network of canals (51:13, 36; Isaiah 44:27). Without water the city could neither live nor be defended.

decisions.choice: carved images ... terrors: idols, mocked as frightening things
decisions.reason: The first word means images carved from wood or stone (8:19; 51:47). The second means terrors or dreadful things (Exodus 15:16); here it is a scornful name for idols, which frighten their worshipers but have no power. Its use for idols is found only here.

decisions.choice: they go mad: they act like people out of their minds
decisions.reason: The verb is used of people raving like madmen, drunk on the cup of God's anger (25:16; 51:7). Babylon's devotion to its idols is a kind of madness.

decisions.choice: idols ... dreadful images (B); idols ... frightening statues (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the carved images as idols and say what the "terrors" are (meaning decision m3).

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן יֵשְׁב֤וּ צִיִּים֙ אֶת־אִיִּ֔ים וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ בָ֖הּ בְּנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־תֵשֵׁ֥ב עוֹד֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁכּ֖וֹן עַד־דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Therefore will dwell desert creatures with hyenas, and will dwell in her daughters of [the] ostrich, and not she will be inhabited again forever, and not she will be settled to generation and generation.
pieces: So desert creatures will live there with hyenas, \q and ostriches will make their home in her. \q She will never be lived in again, \q nor settled through all generations.

L.39: Therefore desert creatures will dwell with hyenas, \q and ostriches will dwell in her; \q she will never again be inhabited, \q nor will she be settled from generation to generation.

R.39: So wild animals of the desert and hyenas will live there. \q Ostriches will live in Babylon. \q No people will ever live there again, \q not for all time to come.

decisions.choice: desert creatures, hyenas, ostriches: wild animals of waste places
decisions.reason: The same animals live in the ruins of Babylon in Isaiah 13:21-22 and of Edom in Isaiah 34:13-14. The first word means creatures of dry places. The second is probably the hyena, though it may be the jackal. "Daughters of the ostrich" is a usual name for the ostrich, though some take it as an owl. The point is that only wild animals will live there.

decisions.choice: never inhabited from generation to generation: as in Isaiah 13:20
decisions.reason: Isaiah spoke of Babylon in the same way: it will never be lived in, from generation to generation (Isaiah 13:20).

decisions.choice: wild animals of the desert; not for all time to come
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain phrase for the desert creatures and for "generation and generation".

records.source: כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֨ת אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־סְדֹ֧ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָ֛ה וְאֶת־שְׁכֵנֶ֖יהָ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: As [the] overthrow [by] God of Sodom and Gomorrah and her neighbors, declares Yahweh, not will dwell there [a] man, and not will sojourn in her [a] son of man.
pieces: As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q no one will live there; \q no human being will settle in it.

L.40: As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q no one will live there, \q and no {{gender:human being|son of man}} will sojourn in it.

R.40: Babylon will be like Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them when God destroyed them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q No one will live there. \q No one will even stay there for a while.

decisions.choice: the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah: the pattern of total destruction
decisions.reason: God's destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24-25) became the picture of a judgment that leaves nothing behind (Deuteronomy 29:22; Amos 4:11; Isaiah 13:19, of Babylon). The same words are said of Edom in 49:18, except that here God is named as the one who overthrew the cities and the LORD "declares" rather than "says".

decisions.choice: stay: live as a sojourner, for a time
decisions.reason: The second verb means to live somewhere as a guest or newcomer. Not only will no one settle there; no one will even stop there.

decisions.choice: a man ... a son of man: any human being
decisions.reason: Both phrases mean any person at all, as in 49:18 and 49:33.

decisions.choice: human being (L, with the gender setting; B)
decisions.reason: The words mean any person, men and women alike, so Literal uses the gender setting with the traditional wording "son of man" as the alternative. The two lines keep the wording of 49:18 at each level, where the Hebrew is the same; Readable puts the comparison into its own sentence.
